x.articleTitle: Graph embeddings you can watch being built
thread: A Terraphim graph embedding is not a vector. It is a node plus its directed edges and integer counters. New interactive page runs the actual Rust terraphim_rolegraph crate, compiled to WASM, in your browser — the same code paths the Rust tests exercise.
Aho-Corasick matching live: type text, watch thesaurus terms fire with concept ids. 'raft quorum consensus' -> #1 raft, #6 quorum, #2 consensus in a single pass.

Index 8 documents step by step: adjacent concept matches become directed edges, counters increment. End state: 10 concepts, 23 edges — including a title-match self-loop that is exactly what Rust's Document::to_string() semantics predict.
Query 'consensus': doc-membership earns 19 = node 7 + edge 1 + doc 2, plus node 7 + edge 1 + doc 1 through a second edge. Every point of the sum is a named node, a named edge, a count.

Honest failures included: 'byzantine fault tolerance' matches no thesaurus term and returns empty while the vector panel still scores. Add a synonym and the automaton rebuild is measured live in single-digit ms.

Compared honestly with node2vec, GCN, TransE, Cleora and API vector DBs across training, update cost, explainability, determinism, memory — plus the hybrid retrieval already implemented (TriggerIndex TF-IDF fallback, BM25 + KG). Try it: https://terraphim.ai/docs/graph-embeddings-interactive/

githubDiscussions.title: Interactive explainer: Terraphim graph embeddings (real Rust crate compiled to WASM)
githubDiscussions.body:
New interactive page: https://terraphim.ai/docs/graph-embeddings-interactive/

A Terraphim graph embedding is a node plus its directed edges and integer counters — not a point in a vector space. The page demonstrates this with the actual terraphim_rolegraph Rust crate compiled to WebAssembly running in the browser: live Aho-Corasick matching over the thesaurus, step-by-step indexing of a real corpus (10 concepts, 23 directed edges), and a query ledger that decomposes every score into named node + named edge + document counts.

Honesty in both directions: out-of-vocabulary queries return an empty set rather than a fuzzy guess, synonym additions trigger a real automaton rebuild measured in milliseconds, and the comparison with node2vec, GCN, TransE, Cleora and dense vector DBs includes where the graph loses. It also references the hybrid retrieval already implemented: query_graph_with_trigger_fallback (TF-IDF trigger index) and search_sessions_hybrid (BM25 + KG boosts).

Everything on screen is the real algorithm — the same code paths the crate's tests exercise.

A Terraphim graph embedding is not a point in a vector space — it is a node plus its directed edges and integer counters. Type text and a real Aho-Corasick automaton returns concept ids; index the corpus step by step and adjacent matches become directed edges (10 concepts, 23 edges); query 'consensus' and the ledger decomposes doc-membership's 19 points into named node + edge + document contributions.

The honesty runs both ways: 'byzantine fault tolerance' returns an empty set rather than a fuzzy answer, and adding a synonym triggers a real automaton rebuild measured in milliseconds. The page compares node2vec, GCN, TransE, Cleora and API vector DBs across update cost, explainability, determinism and memory — and points at the hybrid retrieval already implemented (query_graph_with_trigger_fallback TF-IDF fallback; search_sessions_hybrid BM25 + KG).
